title: In-memory rollback-journal chunks, spill, and lifecycle

scope.rationale: This unit owns the complete active memjournal.c chunk representation, sequential/header writes, cached reads, truncation, cleanup, optional atomic spill to the underlying VFS, open mode selection, identity, and size calculation. The native Journal is a direct source-shaped translation and its chunk/cursor/truncate/spill trace matches the pinned C implementation; production Pager ABI routing and complete failure assurance remain open.
excluded_responsibilities: Pager policy selecting statement or rollback memory journals
Underlying VFS file method behavior after successful spill
Inactive sqlite3JournalCreate compile-profile branch and other inactive branches not present in the behavioral inventory

external_source_responsibilities: Pager journal-open policy and atomic-write call sites
sqlite3_file preallocated-storage ABI owner and exact sqlite3Os wrappers
dependencies.caller_closure: Production Pager owns Journal for rollback creation, header/record writes, sync, playback, close and sqlite3_file control exposure. Focused native callers also exercise memory-only and spill modes through the same v1 ABI owner.

inputs: Allocator, optional underlying sqlite3_vfs/name, open flags, spill threshold, offsets, byte spans, truncate sizes and sync flags
outputs: Exact SQLite result code, read bytes, file size, memory/spilled identity
contracts.ownership: Each in-memory chunk is one allocation containing link plus payload. Journal owns and frees chunks. Successful spill transfers behavior to an owned underlying sqlite3_file allocation; failed spill closes the provisional file and retains every chunk.
contracts.state_and_results: Endpoint and readpoint preserve source cursor semantics. Writes append except the bounded header rewrite and truncate-before-rewrite path. Threshold zero opens the real file immediately, negative remains memory-only, and positive spills when exceeded.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Memjournal has no mutex. In-memory methods perform no I/O. Spill invokes underlying xOpen/xWrite and later routes read/write/truncate/sync/size/close through its method table.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Short reads do not mutate cursors, chunk OOM returns IOERR_NOMEM with a closable prefix, and failed spill preserves in-memory rollback content for continuation.

representation_differences: Flexible C FileChunk payload is represented by one aligned Zig allocation containing a Chunk header followed by chunk_size bytes.
C morphs the caller-preallocated MemJournal bytes into the real sqlite3_file on spill; Zig owns a separate aligned real-file storage slice because the translated Journal is a typed native owner.
The typed Journal embeds a v1 sqlite3_file method table for Pager and file-control integration while retaining separately owned aligned real-file storage after spill.

oracle.protocol: Native tests cross chunk boundaries, repeated/cached reads, short reads, header overwrite, partial and zero truncation, append after truncation, threshold spill through a real VFS method table, size, close, and one-shot chunk OOM. The pinned C/Zig workers emit and compare 14 exact state and byte observations.
oracle.normalization: Bytes, sizes, result codes and ordered method events are exact; allocation addresses are ignored.

assurance.oom: First chunk OOM and cleanup are covered; every chunk boundary and spill-storage/open/write OOM/fault site remains open.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: Successful real-VFS spill and readback pass. Failed-open/write restoration and crash boundaries need exact differential coverage; source unit is single-threaded.
assurance.malformed_input: Short read and forward-gap write are guarded; source relies on internal assertions for several invalid write shapes.
assurance.continuation: Truncate/reappend, close after OOM, and successful spill continuation pass; failed spill retry matrix remains open.
assurance.performance: Chunk traversal and allocation shape follow source. Readpoint caching is retained; benchmark and production pager selection remain open.

integration.native_call_path: Pager rollback path -> Journal embedded sqlite3_file/typed methods -> chunk owner or underlying sqlite3_vfs method table
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Yes. Pager no longer allocates or dispatches rollback-journal sqlite3_file storage directly; Journal owns memory-only, spill, immediate-real, playback, sync and close transport.

independent_review.notes: Requires pinned C differential, complete failure matrix, Pager ABI integration, and independent review.

implementation_spans: upstream/sqlite/src/memjournal.c was reviewed completely, including all FileChunk/FilePoint/MemJournal layout, method-table, read/write/truncate/free/close/sync/size, spill, open-mode, identity and sizing responsibilities
The inactive sqlite3JournalCreate conditional body was inspected for its relationship to memjrnlCreateFile but remains excluded by the selected compile profile

src/core/memory_journal.zig was reviewed completely, including typed chunk allocation, cursor state, atomic spill owner transition, real-file dispatch, and focused tests; every mapped declaration is AST-hashed
callers: Pager and pcache policy select memory-only, spillable statement, or immediate real-file journal handles; atomic-write callers may force materialization in profiles where enabled
The native focused caller invokes Journal directly through production MemoryVfs ABI; Pager still opens its configured VFS journal directly and is an explicit integration blocker
After successful spill, all read/write/truncate/sync/size/close operations dispatch to the underlying sqlite3_file method table
callees: Read rejects ranges past endpoint without cursor mutation, restarts from head unless exact readpoint reuse applies, copies across chunks, and caches the next chunk/end offset only when available

Write spills before mutation when positive threshold is exceeded; otherwise it permits append, initial bounded header overwrite, or truncate-before-rewrite, allocating one linked payload chunk at each boundary

Truncate frees the suffix or whole list, retains the containing final chunk for partial size, moves endpoint, and invalidates readpoint; close frees all memory chunks while sync is a memory no-op and size returns endpoint

CreateFile snapshots the memory owner, opens real storage, writes each chunk with a shortened final write, frees chunks only after complete success, and on any open/write error closes provisional storage and restores the original journal
JournalOpen zeroes storage, opens real VFS immediately for zero threshold, selects threshold-sized chunks for positive spill, and default 1024-byte allocation shape for negative memory-only mode
assertions_branches_cleanup: All 55 behavior IDs cover short/readpoint/head traversal and cross-chunk reads; chunk free; spill open/write/success/restore; spill threshold; append/header/truncate writes; chunk OOM; truncate variants; lifecycle dispatch; open modes; identity and sizing
Every chunk is one owner containing link plus payload; successful spill retires all chunk owners and installs real-file ownership, while failed spill retains byte-identical in-memory rollback content
Chunk allocation failure leaves the already-linked prefix closable and endpoint at the successfully written prefix; failed spill continuation and exhaustive boundary/fault matrices remain blockers
The source module is single-threaded and owns no mutex; all I/O is confined to spill and post-spill method dispatch
